solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stop demolition of side street

indicators.note: a demolished thing is knocked to pieces, so the letters that follow are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone protests against the knocking down of a side street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolition of' rearranges SIDE plus ST into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or leave off doing something, a formal synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Depressing to find beloved embracing Rex

indicators.note: embracing means holding round, so the word for beloved wraps the letter for Rex

parts.note: dear means beloved
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Sadness at finding a loved one in the arms of someone called Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dismal or gloomy.

clue.text: Highy important artist involved in the Spanish uprising

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so the artist goes within the reversed word
in a down clue an uprising reads upwards, so the Spanish word is reversed

parts.note: las is a Spanish word for the (feminine plural)
Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: A major painter takes part in a Spanish revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highy' is a typo for 'Highly'. 'uprising' turns LAS into SAL, which holds EMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work is highly influential, shaping much that follows it.

clue.text: A resounding defeat in Southend's opener at Morecambe caused it

indicators.note: an opener is the first, so only the first letter of Southend is taken

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, so what he caused was laughter

explanation.surface: A football report: Southend take a thrashing in a match at Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend and Morecambe are both English seaside towns with football clubs, but Morecambe here is the comedian. 'in' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughter in sport is a crushing, one-sided defeat.

clue.text: Key to provision of meals on a ship

parts.note: A is a musical key
board is meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Something essential to catering arrangements at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on board a vessel is the plain sense of the adverb, so 'on a ship' fits exactly.

clue.text: It's more than expected for working in public transport

indicators.note: in shows one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bus is public transport
on means working, as in the machine is on

explanation.surface: Getting work done on the bus is an unexpected extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is something extra on top of what was due or anticipated.

clue.text: A container holding mostly cereal and fruit

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the pot goes round the shortened cereal

parts.note: a pot is a container

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rice is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A bowl of cereal with some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts RICE to RIC; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Reportedly rude after princess's speech

indicators.note: after places the rude word behind the princess's

parts.note: Di was Diana, Princess of Wales, so Di's gives DIS

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: coarse means rude or vulgar

explanation.surface: Gossip about a rude remark following a royal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal talk or spoken communication on a subject.

clue.text: Beef, say, about team collapsing against Germany

parts.note: RE is Latin for concerning, used as about
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

indicators.note: a collapsing team falls apart, so its letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A sports report on a team that crumbles in a match against Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' signals the anagram of the second piece; 'against' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is an example of the darker meats from cattle, sheep and the like, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Entrance artist with hint of scent

parts.note: Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the first letter of scent is used

explanation.surface: A painter whose work carries a faint perfume, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like the verb (to delight) but is the noun meaning a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act or means of going in, a formal synonym of entry.

clue.text: Deny lad is worried by envy for example

indicators.note: worried means shaken about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy troubled by jealousy refuses to admit it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried by' signals the rearrangement of DENY, LAD and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the traditional seven cardinal vices of Christian teaching.

clue.text: Misbehave with Hardy heroine having fled to southern Greece

indicators.note: having here means holding within, so the heroine's name wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
fled means ran
GR is the abbreviation for Greece

explanation.surface: A literary heroine misbehaves by running off to the south of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'to' are link words; the heroine's name splits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress is to break a rule or moral law, a stronger synonym of behaving badly.

clue.text: Dog food

definitions.meaning: the ... ... is a Chinese breed of dog

explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses of the word: a Chinese dog breed and slang for grub.

clue.text: Guide's helpful hint about taking in the centre of Toulouse

indicators.note: taking in means containing, so the reversed word holds the middle letters
about signals turning round, so the word for a hint is read backwards

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint

indicators.note: the centre of an eight-letter word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A guidebook entry offering a useful tip about central Toulouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TIP into PIT, and 'the centre of' takes LO from the middle of Toulouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot steers or guides, as a ship's pilot guides vessels into harbour.

clue.text: Over-hasty of priest to get flat set back by river

indicators.note: set back means turned back, so the word for flat is reversed

parts.note: tame means flat or dull, as in a tame ending
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A priest's rush to buy a flat is delayed by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns TAME into EMAT; 'of', 'to get' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Premature means done too soon, before the proper time, which is hasty.

clue.text: Lawyer maintaining the Italian conservative intended to waste time

indicators.note: maintaining means holding up or keeping in, so the lawyer encloses the Italian word

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
il is Italian for the
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A slow lawyer defending an Italian Tory politician by stalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory tactics are designed to cause delay, so the adjective means meant to stall.

clue.text: Much the same as getting very warm quickly

parts.note: like means similar to
hot means very warm

explanation.surface: Something comparable to things heating up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly or without hesitation, as fast as a bullet.

clue.text: Henry and Pat embarrassed to find it's for women only

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being thrown into confusion, so the names' letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Henry and Pat blush when they find they've wandered into a women-only event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassed' rearranges HENRY and PAT; 'and' is no fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen party is a celebration for a bride-to-be and her female friends before the wedding.

clue.text: It's used in defence of soldier brought back in a huff

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a pet is a fit of sulking, as in to be in a pet

explanation.surface: A soldier returns to base in a bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back in' does no work: the two pieces simply join, and the blog likewise finds no reversal to make the clue's wording fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a protective wall on a rampart or bridge, shielding defenders.

clue.text: Coming around in luggage van kidnapped by Jack

indicators.note: coming around means turning back, so the concealed letters are read in reverse
in shows the letters sit within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Someone is snatched by a man called Jack, hidden in a luggage van.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EVANK run across 'luggagE VAN Kidnapped' and 'Coming around' reverses them; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the jack in a pack of playing cards, the picture card below the queen.

clue.text: Rated new company's design style

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A newly rated firm's approach to design.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Moderately good food by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the word is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: fare is food provided, as in good plain fare

explanation.surface: A restaurant critic's lukewarm verdict on a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair as a grade means middling or passable, neither poor nor excellent.

clue.text: Girl, admitting it, sent back on prison ship

parts.note: a brig is a naval prison on a ship

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the name takes in the other piece

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

indicators.note: sent back signals that the little word is turned round

explanation.surface: A girl owns up to something and is shipped back to a prison ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns only the little word, which then sits inside the girl's name; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel, a specific kind of the general class.

clue.text: Dull sounding nobleman

indicators.note: sounding says the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: barren means dull or unproductive

explanation.surface: A tedious aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is the lowest rank of the British peerage.

clue.text: 1 in 18 they say is innocent

indicators.note: in shows the numeral goes inside
they say means spoken, so the silent letter goes

parts.note: the answer to 18 Across, the jack in cards
1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: One of the rogues is, people claim, guileless.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' is the numeral one, not 1 Across; 18 refers to the answer at 18 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means artless or unworldly, lacking guile like an innocent.

clue.text: Backing at an end after last of sponsors left

indicators.note: after places the phrase for at an end behind the letter taken from sponsors
the last of a word is its final letter, here from sponsors

parts.note: up means over or finished, as in time is up
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Funding runs out once the final sponsor withdraws.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing and support both mean help or endorsement given to a cause.

clue.text: An expression of delight at story of cyclist's skilful manoeuvre

parts.note: whee is an exclamation of glee
a story can be a lie, as in telling stories

explanation.surface: A cyclist whoops with joy at the tale of a clever stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelie is a stunt riding a bicycle on its back wheel with the front lifted.

clue.text: Spin out odd piece on former model

indicators.note: on places the odd piece after the earlier pieces in an across answer

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the Model T was Ford's famous car
an end is an odd leftover piece, as in odds and ends

explanation.surface: A fashion model talks at length about a strange piece, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin something out is to prolong it, the same as making it longer.

clue.text: In a book about Hungary

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the book word goes round the letter for Hungary

parts.note: a tome is a large book
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: A guide book covering Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at home means being in, not out, as in 'is she in?'
